questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Operating System Services & System Calls
questions.text: Explain the Dual-Mode Operation of an Operating System (User Mode vs. Kernel / Privileged Mode) with the Mode Bit. What are System Calls? Explain the step-by-step mechanism of executing a system call using hardware interrupts, software traps, and system call interface tables.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Operating System Services & System Calls
questions.text: Compare Monolithic Kernel, Layered Architecture, and Microkernel Architecture with neat diagrams. What are the advantages and disadvantages of a microkernel architecture (e.g. Mach, QNX)?

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Process Management & CPU Scheduling Algorithms
questions.text: Explain the 5-state Process State Transition Diagram (New, Ready, Running, Waiting/Blocked, Terminated). Explain the contents of a Process Control Block (PCB). Differentiate between Short-term, Medium-term, and Long-term Schedulers.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Process Management & CPU Scheduling Algorithms
questions.text: What is a Thread? Differentiate between Process and Thread. Compare User-Level Threads (ULT) vs Kernel-Level Threads (KLT). Describe Multithreading Models: Many-to-One, One-to-One, and Many-to-Many.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Process Management & CPU Scheduling Algorithms
questions.text:
Consider the following set of processes arriving at given arrival times with CPU burst times in milliseconds:
$P_1$: Arrival 0, Burst 8
$P_2$: Arrival 1, Burst 4
$P_3$: Arrival 2, Burst 9
$P_4$: Arrival 3, Burst 5.
Draw Gantt charts and calculate average waiting time and turnaround time for: (a) FCFS, (b) Shortest Job First (SJF Non-preemptive), (c) Shortest Remaining Time First (SRTF Preemptive), and (d) Round Robin (Time Quantum $q = 3\,\text{ms}$).

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Process Management & CPU Scheduling Algorithms
questions.text: Explain Priority Scheduling (Preemptive vs Non-preemptive). What is Starvation / Indefinite Blocking and how does Aging solve it? Explain Multilevel Queue Scheduling and Multilevel Feedback Queue Scheduling.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Process Management & CPU Scheduling Algorithms
questions.text: Define the Critical Section Problem. State the three essential requirements (Mutual Exclusion, Progress, Bounded Waiting) that every critical section solution must satisfy. Explain Peterson's Algorithm for two-process mutual exclusion and prove that it satisfies all three requirements.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Process Synchronization, Semaphores & Deadlocks (Banker)
questions.text: What are Semaphores? Differentiate between Binary Semaphore (Mutex) and Counting Semaphore. Define atomic `wait()` (P) and `signal()` (V) operations. Write a deadlock-free and race-condition-free solution to the Classical Producer-Consumer (Bounded Buffer) Problem using semaphores.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Process Synchronization, Semaphores & Deadlocks (Banker)
questions.text: Implement a starvation-free solution to the Readers-Writers Problem and Dining Philosophers Problem using semaphores and monitors.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Operating System Services & System Calls
questions.text: What is a Deadlock? State and explain the four Coffman Conditions necessary for a deadlock to occur: (1) Mutual Exclusion, (2) Hold and Wait, (3) No Preemption, and (4) Circular Wait.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Operating System Services & System Calls
questions.text: Explain Banker's Algorithm for Deadlock Avoidance. A system has 5 processes ($P_0-P_4$) and 3 resource types ($A, B, C$) with total instances $(10, 5, 7)$. Allocation matrix and Max claim matrix are given. (a) Compute the Need Matrix, (b) Verify if the system is in a safe state and determine the safe sequence, (c) If $P_1$ requests $(1, 0, 2)$, can the request be granted immediately?

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Memory Management, Paging & Virtual Memory (Page Replacement)
questions.text: Explain Contiguous Memory Allocation strategies: First Fit, Best Fit, and Worst Fit. Differentiate between Internal Fragmentation and External Fragmentation. How does Compaction resolve external fragmentation?

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Memory Management, Paging & Virtual Memory (Page Replacement)
questions.text: Explain Paging hardware with Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB). Given a system with page size $4\,\text{KB}$, 32-bit logical address space, and 32-bit physical address space, calculate page table size. Calculate Effective Memory Access Time (EMAT) if TLB hit ratio is $95\%$, TLB access time is $20\,\text{ns}$, and main memory access time is $120\,\text{ns}$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Memory Management, Paging & Virtual Memory (Page Replacement)
questions.text: Explain Hierarchical Paging (Two-level paging), Inverted Page Table, and Segmentation hardware with Segment Table (Base and Limit registers). Compare Paging vs Segmentation.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Memory Management, Paging & Virtual Memory (Page Replacement)
questions.text: What is Virtual Memory and Demand Paging? Explain the step-by-step Page Fault Handling sequence. Calculate Effective Access Time (EAT) under demand paging with page fault service time $8\,\text{ms}$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Memory Management, Paging & Virtual Memory (Page Replacement)
questions.text: Consider the page reference string: $7, 0, 1, 2, 0, 3, 0, 4, 2, 3, 0, 3, 2, 1, 2, 0, 1, 7, 0, 1$. Calculate the number of page faults for a system with 3 memory frames using: (a) FIFO, (b) Optimal (OPT), and (c) Least Recently Used (LRU) page replacement algorithms. What is Belady's Anomaly and which page replacement algorithm exhibits it?

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Operating System Services & System Calls
questions.text: What is Thrashing? What causes thrashing in multiprogramming operating systems? Explain how thrashing is prevented using: (a) Working-Set Model (Locality of reference), and (b) Page Fault Frequency (PFF) strategy.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: File System Organization & Directory Structures
questions.text: Explain File Allocation Methods: (a) Contiguous Allocation, (b) Linked Allocation, and (c) Indexed Allocation (UNIX Inode structure with direct, single indirect, double indirect, and triple indirect pointers). Compare their access speeds and external fragmentation.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Secondary Storage Structure & Disk Scheduling (SCAN, C-SCAN)
questions.text: A magnetic disk drive has 200 cylinders (0 to 199). The read/write head is initially at cylinder 53 moving towards higher cylinders. The pending I/O request queue in FIFO order is: $98, 183, 37, 122, 14, 124, 65, 67$. Calculate total head movements (tracks) and illustrate head trajectory for: (a) FCFS, (b) Shortest Seek Time First (SSTF), (c) SCAN (Elevator algorithm), (d) C-SCAN, and (e) LOOK / C-LOOK.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Secondary Storage Structure & Disk Scheduling (SCAN, C-SCAN)
questions.text: Explain Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) levels: RAID 0 (Striping), RAID 1 (Mirroring), RAID 5 (Block-level striping with distributed parity), and RAID 6 (Dual distributed parity). Compare their storage efficiency, data redundancy, and fault tolerance.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Memory Management, Paging & Virtual Memory (Page Replacement)
questions.text: Explain the role and architecture of Virtual Machines (Type-1 Hypervisor vs Type-2 Hypervisor) and Containers (Docker). What is the difference between Bootstrapping (IPL) and Context Switching?

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Process Management & CPU Scheduling Algorithms
questions.text: Explain Deadlock Detection using Resource Allocation Graphs (RAG) and Wait-For Graphs. Explain Deadlock Recovery strategies: Process Termination and Resource Preemption (Victim selection, Rollback, Starvation).

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Process Management & CPU Scheduling Algorithms
questions.text: Explain Free Space Management techniques on disk: Bit Vector (Bit Map), Linked Free Space List, Grouping, and Counting.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Memory Management, Paging & Virtual Memory (Page Replacement)
questions.text: Explain I/O Hardware principles: Memory-Mapped I/O vs Port-Mapped I/O, Polling (Busy waiting), Interrupt-Driven I/O, and Direct Memory Access (DMA) with cycle stealing.
